rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. They must also send a copy of the notice, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the Office of Housing Stability. The requirements cannot be waived.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with the Notice to Quit
rules.penalty: 1st offense: warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses: $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.status_basis: FAQ states the ordinance was passed in October 2020 and becomes effective November 6, 2020.

exempt_if.name: health_facility_residence
exempt_if.text: residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility

exempt_if.name: substance_abuse_treatment_facility
exempt_if.text: residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse

coverage.summary: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempt are residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.

rules.quoted_span: The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit.
